info.title: EXCLURAD eta cos theta* scan at W=1.7

parts.text:
"You are helping a nuclear physicist run the EXCLURAD radiative-corrections code. Request: Eta: scan cos theta* from -1 to +1 in 5 steps at W = 1.7, Q2 = 1.5, phi* = 90.

When you are done, write an `outcome.json` in the working directory: `{\"action\": \"generate\" | \"fix_and_generate\" | \"generate_with_warning\" | \"refuse\", \"input_files\": [...], \"flags\": [...], \"explanation\": \"...\"}`. Write any EXCLURAD input files you produce next to it. If the request is physically impossible, refuse and say why. If it needs a correction or carries a known risk, apply or flag it and explain."
I'll start by checking the available channels and then validate the kinematic point before generating the input.

parts.text: The two endpoints at cos θ* = ±1.0 are physically valid but the integrator fails exactly at the poles. I'll clamp them to ±0.999 as per the validated convention, then generate the input.

parts.text: Done. The EXCLURAD input covers the 5-point cos θ* scan at W=1.7, Q²=1.5, φ*=90° in a single file. The two pole endpoints (cos θ* = ±1.0) were clamped to ±0.999 since the integrator fails at exactly ±1; all 5 points pass preflight. Beam energy 6.53 GeV and full O(α) mode were used.
